subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt concurrent or re-entrant same-session `ContextEngine.maintain()` calls after an opted-in deferred-maintenance timeout, or preserve engine-side single-flight semantics while still releasing the user-turn lane?
rationale: The host fence protects transcript and task state, but it cannot make arbitrary third-party engine internals, locks, caches, or external side effects safe under a newly permitted concurrent lifecycle.

options.title: Preserve engine serialization
options.body: Keep user-turn recovery at timeout but avoid starting another same-session maintenance invocation until the abandoned worker settles or a separately designed cancellation/serialization contract exists.

options.title: Adopt the concurrent lifecycle
options.body: Accept the documented re-entrant `maintain()` contract and treat engine-local serialization or idempotence as a supported plugin responsibility.

recommendation.title: Preserve engine serialization
recommendation.body: Keep user-turn recovery at timeout but avoid starting another same-session maintenance invocation until the abandoned worker settles or a separately designed cancellation/serialization contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the most direct implementation history for the proposed lifecycle contract; a repository owner still needs to make the acceptance decision.
